$description: Dark-theme colour values for the 'adminlte-classic' template (Classic Admin). This file mirrors tokens/colors.json: for every light value at color.<path> there is a dark value at color.dark.<path>, and nothing else. The light palette in colors.json remains the DEFAULT — this is the override set, not a second independent palette. See foundations/theming.md for how a target stack applies it, and for the three groups that deliberately do NOT appear here. Original document — see ATTRIBUTION.md.

primary.$description: Unchanged from the light theme. A solid fill's contrast obligation is against its own label, not against the page behind it — text.on-accent (white) over this fill is 4.50:1 in either theme. Fills therefore do not need dark counterparts; only their SURROUNDINGS do. Where this accent is used as text rather than as a fill, use color.dark.text.accent.primary, exactly as the light theme uses color.text.accent.primary.

secondary.$description: Unchanged, for the reason given on brand.primary. White over this fill is 4.69:1.

success.$description: Unchanged. White over this fill is 4.53:1.

danger.$description: Unchanged. White over this fill is 4.53:1.

warning.$description: Unchanged, and still takes text.on-accent-dark as a fill, exactly as in the light theme.

info.$description: Unchanged, and still takes text.on-accent-dark as a fill.

light.$description: The neutral pair INVERTS in this theme, because both tokens are defined by their role rather than by their lightness: 'light' means the subtle surface a half-step from the page, used for row hover and section dividers. On a dark page that is a slightly LIGHTER value, not a near-white one — the light theme's #f8f9fa here would be a glaring block. text.primary on this surface is 12.00:1.

dark.$description: The other half of the inversion: 'dark' means the high-contrast fill opposite the page, used for dark chrome and the `dark` Button colour. On a dark page the value that reads as high-contrast is a light one — the light theme's #212529 as a button fill here measures 1.07:1 against surface.canvas and is invisible. NOTE the consequence: this fill takes text.on-accent-dark (13.01:1), where in the light theme it took text.on-accent. Which of the two on-accent tokens an accent pairs with is itself theme-dependent, and this token is where it flips.

canvas.$description: Default background of content surfaces: cards, tables, panels. One step lighter than surface.muted, so a card still reads as raised off the page — in this theme that step, not the shadow, is what carries elevation (see foundations/theming.md).

muted.$description: Background of the content area behind cards/panels. The DARKEST surface in the theme, inverting the light theme's relationship where the page background is darker than the cards only very slightly. Kept a clear step below canvas so the card edge is legible without relying on a shadow.

border.$description: Borders and dividers between surface elements. 1.34:1 against surface.canvas — deliberately a hairline, and deliberately the same property the light theme has (#dee2e6 on #ffffff is 1.30:1). A divider is decoration, not information; the 3:1 non-text obligation lands on focus rings and on any border that is the ONLY thing identifying a control, both of which draw from the accent tokens below, not from this one.

primary.$description: Default body text. 15.43:1 on surface.muted, 13.94:1 on surface.canvas, 12.00:1 on neutral.light. Deliberately not pure white: full-strength white on a near-black surface produces halation that makes long text harder to read, and the ~13:1 this lands at is far above the 4.5:1 floor.

secondary.$description: Supporting text, captions, metadata, placeholders. Verified against every dark surface this template puts text on, the same way the light theme's #687078 was: 5.95:1 on surface.muted, 5.37:1 on surface.canvas, 4.63:1 on neutral.light. Chosen against that worst case — the table hover row — rather than against the card.

inverse.$description: Text on light backgrounds within this theme — which, per the neutral inversion above, is what neutral.dark now is. 15.43:1 on that fill.

link.$description: Text links, matching text.accent.primary as the light theme's link matches its own primary.

on-accent.$description: Unchanged: the accent fills it sits on are unchanged, so the pairing and its measured ratios carry over exactly. Still valid ONLY over brand.primary, brand.secondary, status.success and status.danger.

on-accent-dark.$description: Unchanged, and now used in one MORE place than in the light theme: over status.warning and status.info as before, and additionally over neutral.dark, which has inverted to a light fill. See that token.

accent.$description: The accent colours adjusted to be legible AS TEXT on a dark surface. This group is the exact counterpart of color.text.accent.* in the light theme, and it is the one place where 'dark theme' is not a matter of swapping surfaces: the light theme DARKENS its accents to sit on a light page, so reusing those values here would make every accent text darker than the surface behind it. These are lightened instead. Each value below clears 4.5:1 against all three dark surfaces, verified against the darkest-contrast case (neutral.light, the hover surface). Worth noting: status.warning and status.info — the two the light theme had to darken most heavily, because raw #ffc107 is 1.63:1 and #0dcaf0 is 1.96:1 as text on white — need no adjustment at all here, and are carried over raw at 8.73:1 and 7.27:1. The pairing that fails on light is the one that works on dark, in both directions.

primary.$description: brand.primary as text on dark. 7.57:1 on surface.muted, 6.84:1 on surface.canvas, 5.89:1 on neutral.light. Also the focus-ring colour in this theme: raw brand.primary as a ring measures 3.67:1 against surface.canvas, which clears the 3:1 non-text floor but leaves nothing in hand, and this value is comfortably clear of it.

secondary.$description: brand.secondary as text on dark; the same value as text.secondary, mirroring the light theme where those two are also identical. 5.95:1 / 5.37:1 / 4.63:1.

warning.$description: status.warning as text on dark — the RAW accent, unmodified. 11.22:1 / 10.14:1 / 8.73:1. The light theme needed #8e6a00 here; on dark the untouched value is one of the most legible in the set.

info.$description: status.info as text on dark — likewise the raw accent. 9.34:1 / 8.44:1 / 7.27:1.

sidebar-bg.$description: Background of the side navigation. Kept a step BELOW surface.muted rather than matching it: the sidebar's job is to read as chrome distinct from the content region, and in the light theme it achieved that by being dark against a light page. On a dark page it has to earn that separation the other way, by being darker still.

sidebar-text.$description: Unchanged from the light theme — it was already a light value on a dark bar. 11.14:1 on this theme's sidebar-bg.

sidebar-item-hover-bg.$description: Slightly weaker than the light theme's 0.1 overlay: the bar underneath is darker here, so the same overlay reads as a larger jump.

sidebar-item-active-bg.$description: Deliberately NOT the same value as sidebar-item-hover-bg, unlike the light theme where both are 0.1. On this darker bar the two states need to be told apart, and the light theme's equality was the weaker part of that spec to carry over.

topbar-bg.$description: Background of the top bar. Matches surface.canvas so the bar reads as a content-side surface sitting above the sidebar's darker chrome — the same relationship the light theme's white topbar had.

series-1.$description: First data series. Lightened from the light theme's #0d6efd, which measures 3.16:1 against neutral.light here — over the 3:1 floor for a graphical mark but with nothing spare. This is 5.13:1 at that worst case.

series-2.$description: Second data series, unchanged: 6.68:1 at the worst dark surface, against only 2.07:1 on a light chart surface. The obligation stated in the light theme's description — a legend plus a per-series mark shape or dash, never colour alone — still applies here regardless, because it exists for colour-vision separation, which the theme does not change.

series-3.$description: Third data series, unchanged: 5.54:1 at the worst dark surface. Same legend-and-shape obligation as series-2.

grid.$description: Axis lines, gridlines and tick marks. Same value as surface.border, so chart chrome recedes to the weight of the surrounding dividers — the same relationship the light theme sets up.

sparkline.$description: Compact sparkline line and fill. Matches text.secondary, as in the light theme, so a strip of sparklines reads as supporting detail.

backdrop.$description: Dimming layer behind a modal or offcanvas panel. Built from black rather than from neutral.dark, which has inverted to a LIGHT value in this theme and would brighten the page instead of dimming it — the clearest example of why this set is a mirror of roles rather than a mechanical value swap. Raised from the light theme's 0.5 to 0.6 because a dim over an already-dark page has less room to work with.

accent-shade.$description: Darkening wash over a surface already filled with an accent colour — a Stat Callout's footer strip, a control hovering on a filled surface. Black-based for the same reason as backdrop. The accent fills it lies over are unchanged between themes, so this wash behaves the same way on them.

accent-glyph.$description: Unchanged: it sits on an accent fill, not on the page, and those fills are unchanged. Decorative only, aria-hidden, never load-bearing.

accent-glyph-dark.$description: Unchanged, for the same reason as accent-glyph.
